summary: The generic décalage argument: torsion removal, descent to the derived category, multiplicativity, the Bockstein model and the precise completeness theorems. This is the early homological input to AΩ, saturated Dieudonné theory and Nygaard filtrations; the geometric AΩ arguments remain unread in this packet.

sources.title: Integral p-adic Hodge theory
sources.authors: Bhargav Bhatt, Matthew Morrow, Peter Scholze
readSections: §6.1–6.2, printed pp.49–55, statements and proofs; extracted lines 2980–3358

nodes.title: Décalage of a torsion-free complex
nodes.statement: For an invertible ideal sheaf I in a ringed topos (T,O_T) and a cochain complex C of O_T-modules that is termwise I-torsion-free (I⊗C^i→C^i injective for all i, with image I·C^i), construct (η_I C)^i={x∈C^i : dx∈I·C^{i+1}}⊗_{O_T}I^{⊗i}. The differential is d_C⊗id, which lands in I·C^{i+1}⊗I^{⊗i}≅C^{i+1}⊗I^{⊗(i+1)} (using I⊗C^{i+1}≅I·C^{i+1}) and, because d²=0, in the degree-(i+1) submodule. Locally, if I=(f), it is the subcomplex of C[1/f] consisting of x∈f^i C^i with dx∈f^{i+1}C^{i+1}, with the differential of C[1/f]; in that case η_I(C[1])≅(η_I C)[1] by multiplication by f in each degree.
hypotheses: C is termwise I-torsion-free; negative tensor powers mean the dual invertible sheaf.
proofSteps: Use injectivity of I⊗C^i→C^i to identify its image and factor the differential.
Apply d²=0 to show the factor lands in the required next-degree submodule.
Identify a principal chart with the localized formula; retain the tensor twist rather than choosing a global generator.
acceptance: Check d²=0 and functoriality on chain maps.
Check the principal description in negative as well as nonnegative degrees.

sources.locator: Definition 6.2 and Remark 6.3, p.49; extracted lines 3005–3027
sources.match: The ideal-based definition and local principal identification are given explicitly.

nodes.title: Torsion removed from cohomology
nodes.statement: For every integer i, H^i(η_I C)≅(H^i(C)/H^i(C)[I])⊗I^{⊗i}; here H^i(C)[I] is the kernel of H^i(C)→H^i(C)⊗I^{-1}. Hence η_I preserves quasi-isomorphisms between I-torsion-free complexes.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of the décalage construction.
proofSteps: Identify Z^i(η_I C) with Z^i(C)⊗I^{⊗i}.
Obtain the induced surjection from H^i(C)⊗I^{⊗i}.
Identify its kernel by lifting a boundary one degree lower; the lift condition is exactly annihilation by I.
acceptance: Compute the two-term complex [A --f→ A], with A f-torsion-free.
Keep I^{⊗i} in the natural isomorphism when I has no chosen generator.

sources.locator: Lemma 6.4 and proof, pp.49–50; extracted lines 3028–3053
sources.match: The source identifies cycles, constructs the surjection and computes its kernel.

nodes.title: The derived décalage functor
nodes.statement: η_I descends from strongly K-flat representatives to a functor Lη_I:D(O_T)→D(O_T), compatible with filtered colimits and canonical truncations. It is generally not exact.
hypotheses: A ringed topos and an invertible ideal I.
Existence of strongly K-flat resolutions is a required input, not proved by the torsion calculation.
proofSteps: Use BMS1 Lemma 6.1 to present the derived category by strongly K-flat complexes.
Use the cohomology formula to invert quasi-isomorphisms.

For filtered colimits and canonical truncations the source (Corollary 6.5) states the compatibility without proof; the check compares the explicit complex η_I C with its cohomology formula degreewise on strongly K-flat representatives.
Use the short exact sequence Z/p→Z/p²→Z/p to detect nonexactness for I=(p).

sources.locator: Lemma 6.1, Corollary 6.5 and Remark 6.6, pp.49–50; extracted lines 2998–3004 and 3054–3065
sources.match: The source gives the localization argument and the explicit nonexactness example.

nodes.title: Products through décalage
nodes.statement: Construct the natural lax symmetric monoidal map Lη_I C⊗^L Lη_I D→Lη_I(C⊗^L D). No general claim that this map is an equivalence is made.
hypotheses: A ringed topos and invertible ideal I; strongly K-flat representatives for derived tensor.
proofSteps: On a homogeneous pair of degrees i,j use I^i⊗I^j≅I^{i+j}.
The signed Leibniz identity puts d(x⊗y) in I times the target whenever dx and dy are in I times their next degrees.
Verify compatibility with symmetry, associativity and quasi-isomorphisms before descending the transformation.
acceptance: Check the Koszul sign in the symmetry constraint.
Check compatibility with multiplication on an I-torsion-free differential graded algebra.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.7 and proof, p.50, extracted lines 3067–3080; Lemma 6.13, p.53, extracted lines 3204–3212
sources.match: The proof supplies the actual termwise product and its differential calculation.

nodes.title: Bockstein reduction of décalage
nodes.statement: There is a natural quasi-isomorphism (Lη_I C)⊗^L O_T/I≃(H^i(C⊗^L O_T/I)⊗I^{⊗i},β), where β is induced by 0→I/I²→O_T/I²→O_T/I→0. The right-hand side is a complex with the Bockstein differential, not a graded group with zero differential.
hypotheses: Use a termwise I-torsion-free representative for the explicit map.
proofSteps: For an I-torsion-free complex the underived tensor product with O_T/I represents the derived one (stated in the source proof, p.52, lines 3164–3166; it follows from the resolution 0→I→O_T→O_T/I→0 and injectivity of I⊗C^i→C^i).
Map η_I C modulo I to cohomology modulo I by sending a representative to its residue cocycle.
Identify the differential on the target with the boundary from reduction modulo I².
Reduce the quasi-isomorphism proof to degree zero by shifting and twisting.
For injectivity lift a Bockstein boundary one degree lower and check the error lies in I·η_I C.
For surjectivity lift a class killed by β to a class modulo I²; the lift defines a cocycle modulo I in η_I C.
acceptance: Verify β²=0 and functoriality of the comparison.
Compare the multiplicative map with the cup product when C comes from a differential graded algebra.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.12 and proof, pp.52–53; extracted lines 3148–3202
sources.match: The two lifting arguments prove the stated comparison with its differential.

nodes.title: Décalage preserves derived completeness
nodes.statement: If C is derived J-complete, then Lη_I C is derived J-complete. This is a preservation result; it does not assert that Lη_I commutes with completion at an unrelated ideal J.
hypotheses: The ringed topos T is replete.
J is a locally finitely generated ideal; I is invertible.
proofSteps: Use the completeness criterion on cohomology modules and the Serre-subcategory property: BMS1 Lemma 6.15, quoted there from [11, Proposition 3.4.4, Lemma 3.4.14] (Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-étale topology for schemes) and recorded here as a DD.1 requirement.
Express H^i(C)[I] as a kernel between derived J-complete modules; use locality for the invertible twist.
Apply closure under cokernels to the torsion quotient and then the criterion on cohomology.
acceptance: Retain repleteness and local finite generation in the exported statement.
Keep the preservation statement distinct from a natural commutation equivalence.

sources.locator: §6.2 opening hypotheses; Lemmas 6.15 and 6.19, pp.53–55; extracted lines 3233–3256 and 3326–3333
sources.match: The source proves preservation by kernel/cokernel closure and explicitly rejects unrestricted commutation.

nodes.title: Completion at the décalage ideal
nodes.statement: For the derived I-completion Ĉ of C, the natural maps completion_I(Lη_I C)→Lη_I(Ĉ)→Rlim_n Lη_I(C⊗^L O_T/I^n) are quasi-isomorphisms.
hypotheses: I is an invertible ideal sheaf locally free of rank one.
proofSteps: Use preservation of derived completeness to construct the first map.
Localize to I=(f) and test equivalences modulo f on derived f-complete complexes.

All three complexes are derived f-complete (Ĉ by construction, Lη_I Ĉ by the preservation lemma, the R lim as a limit of derived complete complexes), and a map of derived f-complete complexes is a quasi-isomorphism once it is one modulo f; the source uses this derived Nakayama step (p.55, lines 3344–3346) without citation.
For the first map apply the Bockstein model, since C/f≃Ĉ/f with the same Bockstein.
For the second map use that D→{D⊗^L O_T/f^n}_n is a pro-quasi-isomorphism for an O_T/f-module complex D.
acceptance: Verify the maps, including their direction, against the I-adic inverse-limit model.
Account separately for derived Nakayama and the pro-quasi-isomorphism input before declaring the proof executable.

sources.match: The source proves both maps by reduction and the pro-system calculation.

gaps.title: Resolution existence behind the derived functor
gaps.detail: BMS1 Lemma 6.1 (p.49, lines 2998–3004) reduces to Stacks Tag 077J. Review R2 read Tag 077J (Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.17.10, public page, 2026-09-15): for any complex G• of O-modules on a ringed site there are bounded-above complexes K_n• whose terms are direct sums of modules j_{U!}O_U, with termwise split injections K_n•→K_{n+1}• and colim K_n•→G• a quasi-isomorphism; its proof cites Modules on Sites Lemma 18.28.8, Derived Categories Lemma 13.29.1 and exactness of filtered colimits. Strong K-flatness of colim K_n• (BMS1's parenthetical) additionally needs flatness of j_{U!}O_U, K-flatness of bounded-above complexes of flat modules and of filtered colimits of K-flat complexes; those auxiliary Stacks lemmas and the exact enhanced-sheaf supplier (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1) have not been read.

gaps.title: Completion foundations and pro-system input
gaps.detail: BMS1 quotes its reference [11, §3.4] (Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-étale topology for schemes, Astérisque 369) for the replete-topos completeness criterion and the Serre-subcategory closure properties (Lemma 6.15) and for the R lim Koszul model of derived completion (p.53, lines 3237–3246); none of [11] was read. Lemma 6.20 also uses, without citation, derived Nakayama for derived f-complete complexes (p.55, lines 3344–3346) and the pro-quasi-isomorphism D→{D⊗^L O_T/f^n}_n for complexes of O_T/f-modules (lines 3351–3353). These are recorded DD.1 requirements; neither a new proof nor an implementation claim is substituted.
